clue.text: Breasted a wave a swift white one?

indicators.note: to wave something is to shake it about, so these letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse breasts a wave, cutting through the water like a swift white creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wave' signals the anagram of BREASTED A. The definition is a hint: an Arab horse is famous for speed and is often grey or white.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabian horses are prized for speed and are often pale grey or white, so a swift white horse is an example.

clue.text: Danced to piped music?

parts.note: a Scottish country dance is often performed to the bagpipes, so dancing to piped music is doing that particular dance

explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish dance usually played on bagpipes, so the past tense names dancing it.

clue.text: A spirit marketed with anonymity?

parts.note: an unnamed product in advertising is 'brand X' or '...', so a spirit sold anonymously could be called by that label

explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine; split in two it reads as an anonymous 'brand Y' in a sales pitch.

clue.text: Prickly situation of New York when a Thunderer's taken over

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece put over another sits above it, so this god's name comes first

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A prickly political situation arises in New York when a thunderous figure takes over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thorny is covered in spikes, i.e. prickly; it also means awkward or difficult.

clue.text: Bring up train

definitions.meaning: to bring up a child is to raise and school them
to train someone is to teach and instruct them

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean teaching or raising: you school a child as you bring it up, and instruction is training.

clue.text: Having a fine blow-out but the account remains unsettled

parts.note: a bill is an account of money due
a debt still owing is one not yet settled

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a lavish night out but leaves the bill unpaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow-out' suggests a feast; here it is a sail swelling out in a fine wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Sails billowing swell outwards as the wind blows them, so they are having a fine blow-out.

clue.text: Ally embroiled with wild march of tears

indicators.note: embroiled means mixed up and wild means out of control, telling us to jumble these two words together

explanation.surface: A friend is caught up in a wild protest march that ends in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroiled with wild' signals an anagram of ALLY and MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachrymal is the anatomical adjective for weeping, as in the gland that produces teardrops.

clue.text: Bode M.O. ill, and wasn't in as the big guns spoke

indicators.note: ill means badly, so these letters are put together badly, out of order

parts.note: someone who is not in is out

explanation.surface: A medical officer foresees trouble and is out while the artillery thunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' signals the anagram of BODE plus MO, giving BOOMED; 'and' just joins it to OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: When heavy artillery fires it makes a deep resounding noise, which is how the big guns speak.

clue.text: A Gilbertian Emperor or Kadi crushed by a medical man

indicators.note: the letters are held by the doctor, wrapped inside the abbreviation for him

parts.note: MO stands for medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: something crushed is squashed out of shape, so the letters of this word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Muslim judge, or an emperor, is crushed under a doctor in a Gilbert and Sullivan scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' signals the anagram of the judge's title; 'by' sets it inside the doctor. A kadi is a judge in Islamic law; 'or' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado is the Japanese emperor in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera of that name.

clue.text: He pedantically thinks his duty is to

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'He pedantically thinks his duty is to', looks cut short after 'to' (the verb, probably 'teach', is missing); no scan to restore it.
annotationWithheld.clue: He pedantically thinks his duty is to

clue.text: Not very fresh meat for a community in Lancashire

parts.note: food that is old is stale, not fresh
ham is a cured meat

explanation.surface: Stale meat is served up to a town in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: OLDHAM is a mill town near Manchester, historically in the county of Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldham is a large town in north-west England, part of historic Lancashire.

clue.text: Listen, someone wants to borrow that organ

definitions.meaning: to pay attention to what is said

definitions.text: someone wants to borrow that organ
definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase is a request to loan someone the hearing organ

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means pay attention; read literally, it asks you to loan out the organ of hearing.

clue.text: Had influence over dressed kid, we hear

indicators.note: the phrase tells us the word is said aloud and the answer is spelt to match its sound

parts.note: suede is leather, often kidskin, dressed to a soft napped finish

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed child was persuasive, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' is goatskin leather, not a child; dressed kid is suede.
explanation.definitionFit: To sway people is to persuade or influence them.

clue.text: An unadorned testimony of a mason's art?

definitions.text: An unadorned testimony of a mason's art?

parts.words: An unadorned testimony of a mason's art?
parts.note: a builder's work with no decoration or openings stands as plain proof of his craft

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a plain wall without windows or doors, figuratively an impassable obstacle.

clue.text: Showed a blustering walk and a sort of greed carrying the loot

indicators.note: the stolen goods are carried at the front of the rearranged word, so they come first

parts.note: swag is slang for stolen goods

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant of it, so this word appears in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A greedy thief strutted along carrying the stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' signals an anagram of the vice, and 'carrying' means the loot leads, ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To strut is to walk with an arrogant, boastful air.

clue.text: Yield over a crooked deal, for others to follow

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits over the rest

parts.note: to yield is to give way

indicators.note: something crooked is bent out of line, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders over a dishonest business deal so that others may follow suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To set an example or show the way is to offer a path that others can follow.

clue.text: The main point in General Booth's army .

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: William Booth founded the Salvation Army, abbreviated SA
E is a point of the compass, east

explanation.surface: The chief point in the Salvation Army's founder's mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the ocean in old poetry. Booth was the first General of the Salvation Army.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The main' is an old poetic name for the open ocean.

clue.text: Determined group

definitions.meaning: a collection of things belonging together

explanation.definitionFit: Being fixed in purpose is one sense; a collection, as of tools or people, is the other.

clue.text: Parliamentary rep coming under a power unit

indicators.note: in a down answer the later piece sits under the earlier one

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament comes under the control of an energy company.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampere measures electric current, so it is an electrical unit.

clue.text: … evident when it's re treated

parts.note: follows on from the previous clue about the ocean: the shore state seen once the water has drawn back

explanation.definitionFit: When the sea ebbs back from the shore, the water is at its lowest level.

clue.text: Man with gout ordered the first sandwich

indicators.note: the letters are put in a fresh order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man with gout orders the original sandwich in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' signals the anagram of MAN and GOUT. John Montagu, Earl of Sandwich, gave his title to the snack.
explanation.definitionFit: John Montagu was the first Earl of Sandwich, so he is the first holder of that title.

clue.text: A minor strike in Barnstaple

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the town name

explanation.surface: A small industrial stoppage takes place in a Devon town.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNSTAPLE is a town in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: A light blow or knock is a gentle hit.

clue.text: A build-up of a model working community

definitions.text: A build-up of a model working community

parts.words: A build-up of a model working community
parts.note: a mound heaped up by a colony of industrious insects, held up as a model of hard work

explanation.definitionFit: The mound is raised by insects famed for diligence, whose colony is the model of a working society.

clue.text: Get back gun first, it could be worth its weight in gold

definitions.text: it could be worth its weight in gold

indicators.note: the reversed weapon is put at the front, ahead of the other word
the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Retrieve your gun before anything else; it might be worth a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get back' looks like a phrase meaning retrieve, but 'back' goes with the weapon and 'first' puts the turned weapon ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump of gold found in nature is valued literally by its weight.

clue.text: A portion each

parts.note: a piece is a portion or part

explanation.definitionFit: Priced at so much per item means each one costs that.

clue.text: 500 males dance for the young miss

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: the letters dance about into a new order

explanation.surface: Five hundred men dance with a young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A damsel is an old word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: A sign of a vote going to the other side

parts.note: a voter marks the ballot paper with an X, a cross

explanation.surface: A voter changes sides at the ballot box.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving from one side to the opposite one means traversing, passing over.

clue.text: Halt! Look out! It's necessary to time the speedsters

definitions.text: It's necessary to time the speedsters

parts.note: to halt is to stop
to watch is to look out or keep guard

explanation.surface: A race marshal shouts warnings while racers whizz past.
explanation.definitionFit: A timer you start and halt by hand is what officials use to clock racers.

clue.text: A feeble-sounding periodical

indicators.note: the word is said aloud and spelt to match

parts.note: weakly means sickly, feeble

explanation.surface: A thin, flimsy magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine or paper published every seven days is a periodical.

clue.text: T may be amusing, but takes longer to get to the point

definitions.text: takes longer to get to the point
definitions.meaning: a detour off the usual road takes extra time to reach a place

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an entertaining pastime; the other is a road detour that lengthens a journey.

clue.text: A drift off course that could make one eye law differently

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a different way

explanation.surface: A ship drifting off course could make someone view maritime law in a new light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' signals the anagram of EYE and LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is the sideways drift of a ship blown downwind of its course.

clue.text: Sandman didn't call on such a night

definitions.text: Sandman didn't call on such a night

parts.words: Sandman didn't call on such a night
parts.note: the sandman of folklore brings sleep, so if he stays away the night passes awake

explanation.definitionFit: The folklore figure brings slumber; a night without him is one spent wakeful.
